earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only wordlists and Loski & Loski 1989 lexicostatistic survey of Eastern Seram; no grammar/phonology of Bati (Indonesia) exists.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2026. The Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste: Unravelling their prehistory and classification (Languages of the New Guinea Region 1). Berlin: Language Science Press. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18323007. 948 pp.
sources.note: No Bati-specific statement; Bati data come only from Wallace 1869 and Ellen 1993 (Appendix A.8, p. 742). Regional generalisations only: p. 115 'While penultimate stress is the normal rule for Wallacean languages, words with penultimate schwa can have stress on other syllables'; p. 444 (Seram-Tanimbar-Bomberai chapter) 'Stress and/or tone is probably contrastive in some of the Bomberai languages, though the most common pattern in our data is penultimate stress/high tone.' Reproduces Wallace's accented Bati forms (bóia, lúme, wúan, kaúfei, mofánas, fúdia, faasí).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid bati1253 (page and JSON record).
sources.note: Bibliography lists only Wallace 1869 and Turner 1884 wordlists plus overviews; zero descriptive references; alternative name Gah; subclassification per Loski & Loski 1989.

sources.citation: Erniati & Dendi Wijaya. 2023. Korespondensi bunyi bahasa-bahasa daerah di Kabupaten Seram Bagian Timur. KOLITA 21, 84-88. DOI 10.25170/kolita.21.4838.
sources.note: Nothing; sound correspondences among Waru, Utta, Uma, Salas, Kilimoy, Hoti, Geser, Dawang, Banggoi. Bati is not among the languages sampled.

sources.citation: Loski, Russell A. & Gail M. Loski. 1989. The languages indigenous to Eastern Seram and adjacent islands. In Wyn D. Laidig (ed.), Maluku (Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 6), 103-141. Ambon: Pattimura University & SIL.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: Nothing. Lexicostatistic survey; Bati section (§3.7.1, pp. 126-128) lists four segmental correspondences with Geser-Gorom (final high-vowel metathesis susu~suis-a, g~ng, r~l, final i~u) and 3,500 speakers; the words stress/accent/tone/prosody do not occur anywhere in the paper.

sources.citation: Wallace, Alfred R. 1869. The Malay Archipelago, vol. II. London: Macmillan. Appendix 'Languages', pp. 470-475ff; vocabulary no. 42 'Gah — Alfuros of East Ceram' (= Bati).
sources.note: Wordlist only. General convention on p. 471: 'Long, short, and accented syllables are marked in the usual way.' The Gah column carries accent marks (the only primary stress data on Bati) but no statement about placement; the archive.org scanned of the tables is too poor to read the accents.
No phonology; cites Loski & Loski 1989 (with SIL archive id 37441), Grimes & Edwards 2026, and Pelupessy 2012 p. 10 for the endonym Minakyesu 'mountain language'.

sources.citation: Pelupessy, Pieter Jacob. 2012. Esuriun orang Bati. Salatiga: Universitas Kristen Satya Wacana (xxx+503 pp., ISBN 9789791790567).
